chunk_findings.detail: The reuse guard assumes the lower bound of a job's `git_ref` is a hex-sha prefix of `mb`, but nothing in the diff enforces that, and the guard silently drops legitimate same-review jobs, which re-enqueues the sha — the exact duplicate-job bug the change claims to close ("one sha is never enqueued twice"). Concretely: (a) three-dot ranges are common for "diff this branch against base", and `"abc123...def456".rsplit("..", 1)[0]` yields `"abc123."` (trailing dot retained), so `mb.startswith("abc123.")` is `False`; (b) the module's own CLI default is `--base main` (docstring line 11), and if the recorded start is that base name, `start="main"` fails the `len(start) >= RR._MIN_ABBREV` arm outright (while a longer name such as `"develop"` passes, making behavior depend on base-name length); (c) any `HEAD..sha` or `origin/main..sha` form likewise fails. In all of these cases `_reusable_job` returns `None` even though a matching queued/running/done job exists, so the caller enqueues a second job for the same sha and the timeout/re-run path still records `unavailable` instead of collecting the existing job. Reproduce with `jobs=[{"job_type":"review","status":"queued","git_ref":"main..abc1234","id":1}]`, `sha="abc1234"`, `mb=<merge-base sha>`: the job is skipped.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/roborev_branch.py:106 (`_reusable_job`, the `start = ref.rsplit("..", 1)[0] ...` / `mb.startswith(start)` guard)

chunk_findings.detail: The regex `r"Workers:\s*\d+/(\d+)"` returns the number after the slash, i.e. the configured max, not the number of workers actually draining the queue. The intent records the observed state as "4 workers active although config says max_workers=6"; for a `status` line `Workers: 4/6` this helper returns 6 and `queue_position` divides by 6. With only 4 active workers, a job in queue position 5 is actually in wave 2, but the ETA is computed as wave 1, so the queue-aware wait signal is too short and the gate can make wait/re-run decisions as if the queue were moving faster than it is.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/roborev_branch.py:_workers

chunk_findings.detail: The dedupe check is not atomic. Two concurrent `run()` calls for the same HEAD can both execute `job = _reusable_job(_list(exe, where), head, mb)` before either calls `roborev review`. Both see `job is None`, then both invoke `roborev review --since mb`, enqueueing duplicate jobs for the same sha. This is the exact duplicate-job failure the change intends to prevent (e.g. duplicate jobs 3067/3068 for one sha), because nothing serializes the list+enqueue interval.
